quotes.text: SharePoint isn't failing anyone. It's the lack of intentional design that fails SharePoint. The platform offers powerful tools for content structure, governance, and life cycle management.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the usual blame on SharePoint as a design and governance failure.

quotes.text: If content lacks clear structure or metadata, AI systems can only return inconsistent results. They might surface outdated policies or irrelevant files, which undermines trust in the entire platform.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Links content hygiene directly to the quality of AI answers.

quotes.text: Fixing SharePoint is never just an it project. It's a combined effort where a governance sets the rules, automation handles the routine, and training makes it usable for everyone.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the three-part recipe for a lasting fix.

quotes.text: SharePoint doesn't fail companies. Companies fail SharePoint when they skip structure, ignore ownership, and forget life cycle management.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise closing thesis of the episode.

quotes.text: Metadata allows information to carry meaning beyond its storage path. Tag a document with details like department, topic, or approval status, and suddenly search works with precision.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, practical explanation of why metadata beats folders.

chapters.title: Making the fix stick: governance and training
One point of truth and Copilot readiness

takeaways: SharePoint becomes a digital junkyard when organizations treat it as storage without structure, ownership or lifecycle rules.
Clear navigation, content lifecycle practices and consistent metadata turn scattered files into a searchable, trusted knowledge base that Copilot can use.
Lasting success needs governance, automation, champions and continuous measurement, running SharePoint like a product rather than a one-time project.
hook: Duplicate files, outdated policies and search results nobody trusts make SharePoint feel broken. This episode shows IT leaders and knowledge owners why the real problem is missing structure, ownership and lifecycle discipline, and how to turn SharePoint into a single source of truth that is ready for Copilot.
